## Answer

**Top 5 NPM packages by GitHub stars (latest release version per distinct package):**

| # | Package (Name) | Version | GitHub stars | Source repo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `@dmrvos/infrajs>0.0.5>typescript` | 2.6.2 | 94,931 | microsoft/typescript |
| 2 | `@dmrvos/infrajs>0.0.6>typescript` | 2.6.2 | 94,931 | microsoft/typescript |
| 3 | `@dylanvann/svelte` | 3.25.4 | 73,499 | sveltejs/svelte |
| 4 | `@dumc11/tailwindcss` | 0.4.0 | 73,464 | tailwindcss/tailwindcss |
| 5 | `@dollarshaveclub/cli>1.0.0>lodash` | 4.17.4 | 57,779 | lodash/lodash |

Note: rank 5 is a tie — 95 distinct lodash path-style package names all map to `lodash/lodash` and therefore all have 57,779 stars; the alphabetically first is shown. Ranks 1–2 are also tied at 94,931 (two distinct package names pointing at `microsoft/typescript`).

If instead one collapses to **one package per repository**, the top five would be: microsoft/typescript → `@dmrvos/infrajs>0.0.6>typescript` 2.6.2 (94,931); sveltejs/svelte → `@dylanvann/svelte` 3.25.4 (73,499); tailwindcss/tailwindcss → `@dumc11/tailwindcss` 0.4.0 (73,464); lodash/lodash → a lodash path name 4.17.4 (57,779); semantic-org/semantic-ui → `@dreampie/semantic-ui` 2.2.11 (51,069).

## Assumptions

1. **Scope:** `System = 'NPM'` in `packageinfo` (only NPM exists in that table) and `project_packageversion`.
2. **Latest release:** For each distinct `Name`, the row with the highest `VersionInfo.Ordinal` among rows where `VersionInfo.IsRelease = true`. This was used rather than `UpstreamPublishedAt`, because the timestamp is NULL for a large share of release rows (e.g., all `typescript` path packages), while `Ordinal` is populated and is clearly the per-package version ordering. 15,811 distinct NPM package names have at least one release.
3. **Join:** `packageinfo` ↔ `project_packageversion` on `System`, `Name`, `Version` (exact). Only the latest-release version that actually appears in `project_packageversion` can be ranked.
4. **Project info:** `project_info` has no `ProjectName` column, so the repository (`owner/repo`) was parsed from `Project_Information` (e.g., “The project `<owner/repo>` …”, “The GitHub project named …”, “The project is hosted on GitHub under the name …”). All 770 rows yielded a distinct repo path, and the join to `ProjectName` is exact. Stars were parsed from the same text (handling “N stars”, “1 star”, and “stars count of N”).
5. **Package identity:** “Distinct package” = distinct `Name` value as stored. Note that this dataset stores some package names in lockfile-path form (e.g., `@dmrvos/infrajs>0.0.5>typescript`, `@dollarshaveclub/cli>1.0.0>lodash`); these are valid `Name` values in both tables and were treated literally. The exact canonical names (`typescript`, `lodash`, `tailwindcss`, etc.) are not present as plain names anywhere in the database.
6. **Exclusions caused by the data:** `mui-org/material-ui` (89,398 stars) drops out because its only mapped package, `@docly/web`, has latest release 0.2.3, which is not present in `project_packageversion` (that table only has up to 0.2.1). Similarly strapi/rails mappings have no matching latest release version.

## Answer

Following the documented join path (NPM rows in `packageinfo` → `project_packageversion` on System/Name/Version → `project_info`), taking each **distinct NPM `Name`** at its latest **release** version, the top 5 by GitHub stars are:

| # | Package (`Name` as stored) | Version | GitHub stars | Repository |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `@dmrvos/infrajs>0.0.5>typescript` | 2.6.2 | 94,931 | microsoft/typescript |
| 2 | `@dmrvos/infrajs>0.0.6>typescript` | 2.6.2 | 94,931 | microsoft/typescript |
| 3 | `@dylanvann/svelte` | 3.25.4 | 73,499 | sveltejs/svelte |
| 4 | `@dumc11/tailwindcss` | 0.4.0 | 73,464 | tailwindcss/tailwindcss |
| 5 | `@dollarshaveclub/cli>1.0.0>lodash` | 4.17.4 | 57,779 | lodash/lodash |

**Rolled up by underlying package/repository** (which is what "packages" means to a human — see caveat below):

| # | Package | Version | GitHub stars |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | typescript | 2.6.2 | 94,931 |
| 2 | svelte | 3.25.4 | 73,499 |

| 5 | semantic-ui | 2.2.11 | 51,069 |

## Assumptions & notes

1. **"Latest release version"**: a version with `VersionInfo.IsRelease = true`; I picked the maximum `UpstreamPublishedAt`, tie‑broken by maximum `Ordinal`. Using max `Ordinal` alone changes the selection for 153 of the 15,811 released package names, but none of them is in the top rows above (all shown packages have a single release or an agreeing ordinal/date ordering).
2. **Join**: exact equality on `System`, `Name`, `Version` between `packageinfo` and `project_packageversion` (both are NPM-only), then `ProjectName` matched to the repository name embedded in `project_info.Project_Information`. Stars were parsed from that text with patterns like "N stars", "stars count of N", and "starred by N users"; 769/770 descriptions parsed successfully (the one failure, `nandorojo/dripsy` at 1,835 stars, was handled by the third pattern). All rows show 0 fan-out (each package version maps to exactly one project).
3. **Important data caveat**: the NPM `Name` column does not contain plain package names — it contains either scoped names (`@scope/pkg`) or dependency-path keys of the form `root>rootVersion>dependency` (10,941 of 16,614 distinct names). Under the literal `Name`-based definition, `typescript@2.6.2` appears as two "distinct packages" (two different dependents' paths) and **rank 5 is a 95-way tie**: 95 distinct path-named packages map to `lodash/lodash` with 57,779 stars (versions 4.17.4, 4.17.5 and 4.17.11). I broke that tie alphabetically (`@dollarshaveclub/cli>1.0.0>lodash`, 4.17.4); any of the 95 could legitimately occupy rank 5. That is why I also give the repository-level roll-up.
4. **Coverage**: 16,614 distinct NPM names / 661,372 rows in `packageinfo`; 15,811 names have at least one release; 625 latest-release package versions map to a project with ≥1,000 stars (133 such projects), which is sufficient scope to fix the top 5.
5. Projects with more stars but no qualifying package are excluded because no package's *latest release* maps to them — notably `mui-org/material-ui` (89,398 stars), `strapi/strapi` (57,236), `rails/rails` (55,319, not an NPM package), and `microsoft/typescript`'s sibling `typescript-website` (2,019).

## Assumptions

1. **"Distinct NPM package" = distinct `packageinfo.Name`** for `System='NPM'`. In this dataset names include scoped fork names (`@docly/web`, `@dylanvann/svelte`) and dependency-path style names (`parent>version>dep`); there are no plain unscoped names such as `lodash`.
2. **"Latest release version"** = among the package's records that are both `VersionInfo.IsRelease = true` and match a `project_packageversion` row on (`System`, `Name`, `Version`), the one with the highest `VersionInfo.Ordinal` (equivalent here to the latest `UpstreamPublishedAt`). Applying the release filter before the join instead (latest release overall, then join) would drop `@docly/web` (its latest release 0.2.3 is not linked to mui-org/material-ui), letting `lodash` (57,779) into the top 5 in its place.
3. **Stars** are parsed from `project_info.Project_Information`, which has no key column, so the project name is extracted with a regex and stars with the patterns "N stars", "stars count of N", "star count of N", and "starred by N users". 770/770 rows yielded a star value; 767 project names matched `project_packageversion`.
4. **Duplicates removed**: `packageinfo` stores every row twice, so results were deduplicated.
5. Packages whose linked versions are all pre-releases (e.g. `strapi/strapi` 57,236 and `rails/rails` 55,319) are excluded because no release version exists for them.

Row 5 above is the alphabetically-first of that tie; any of the 95 is equally valid.

If packages are collapsed to one entry per **repository**, the top 5 become: **typescript** (2.6.2, 94,931) → **svelte** (3.25.4, 73,499) → **tailwindcss** (0.4.0, 73,464) → **lodash** (95 package ids, versions 3.x–4.17.x, 57,779) → **moment** (33 package ids, versions 2.20–2.24, 47,549).

## How I got there

1. `package_database.packageinfo` (SQLite, 661,372 rows, NPM only): de-duplicated identical rows, parsed `VersionInfo` JSON, kept `IsRelease = true`, and ranked by `VersionInfo.Ordinal` to get one latest release version per distinct `Name` → 15,811 names.
2. `project_database.project_packageversion` (DuckDB): joined on `System`/`Name`/`Version` with `RelationType = 'SOURCE_REPO_TYPE'` (source repo, not issue tracker) → `ProjectName`.
3. `project_database.project_info`: stars were parsed out of the free-text `Project_Information` (patterns "N stars", "stars count of N", "starred by N users", commas stripped — several repos are written as e.g. "73,499 stars" and "a stars count of 94931").
4. Ranked matched packages by stars descending (`ORDER BY stars DESC, Name`), 5 rows, no NULLs, no fan-out on `(Name, Version)`.

## Assumptions / caveats

- **"Latest release version"** = the version with the highest `VersionInfo.Ordinal` among rows where `VersionInfo.IsRelease = true`, per distinct `Name`. `Ordinal` (deps.dev's version-ordering index) was used because `UpstreamPublishedAt` is NULL/`nan` for many rows and, in 154 packages, ordering by publish date disagrees with the version ordering.
- **"NPM package"** = the `Name` values as stored in `packageinfo` (all 16,614 names, `System='NPM'`). Note this dataset contains **no plain** `typescript`, `lodash`, `svelte`, `react`, etc.; 5,590 of the names are dependency-path identifiers of the form `parent>version>dependency`, which is why the top entries look unusual. Excluding those path-style names (arguably not real registry packages) would instead give: `@dylanvann/svelte` 3.25.4 (73,499), `@dumc11/tailwindcss` 0.4.0 (73,464), `@dothq/styled-components` 1.0.0 (39,660), `@dynasty/styled-components` 3.2.1 (39,660), `@ec-nordbund/leaflet` 1.7.1-436430db… (38,715).
- **Star data coverage**: only 770 of the 8,381 projects referenced by `project_packageversion` have `Project_Information` text. Packages whose source repo is outside that set have no star count and cannot be ranked (e.g. `quilljs/quill`, `mobxjs/mobx` have no mapped package at all; `mui-org/material-ui` 89,398, `strapi/strapi` 57,236 and `rails/rails` 55,319 have mapped packages whose latest release version is not in the version-to-project mapping, so they drop out).
- Ties at 57,779 are inherent to the data (one repo, many package identifiers); the 5th row depends on tie-breaking.

## Assumptions

1. **Latest release version**: for each distinct `Name`, the version with `VersionInfo.IsRelease = true` and the highest `VersionInfo.Ordinal` (ties broken by `UpstreamPublishedAt`). 15,811 of the 16,614 NPM names have at least one release version; the other 803 have only prereleases and were excluded.
2. **Package identity** = `Name` as stored, which in this dataset includes dependency-path names like `parent>version>leaf` (e.g. `@dollarshaveclub/cli>1.0.0>lodash`). These are distinct rows in both `packageinfo` and `project_packageversion`. If instead one collapses to the underlying library/repo, the ranking would be: typescript 2.6.2 (94,931), svelte 3.25.4 (73,499), tailwindcss 0.4.0 (73,464), lodash 4.17.4 (57,779), moment 2.20.1 (47,549).
3. **Package→project join**: `System`, `Name`, `Version` matched across databases, restricted to `ProjectType = 'GITHUB'` and `RelationType = 'SOURCE_REPO_TYPE'` (the source-repository relation); using all relation types gives the same top 5.
4. **`project_info` join**: the table has no key column, so the `owner/repo` name was extracted from the `Project_Information` text (770 unique repos) and the star count parsed from the same sentence (four phrasings cover all 770 rows).
5. Ordinal-based and publish-time-based "latest" disagree for only 153 of 15,811 packages and none of the top 5.

## How I got there

1. `project_info.Project_Information` has no key column, so I extracted the repo name from the text (`owner/repo`); 767 of 770 rows matched a `ProjectName` in `project_packageversion` (the 3 exceptions have ≤ 24 forks), and parsed fork counts from the prose (handling `5,782 forks`, `forked 1,277 times`, `forks count of 988`, and thousands separators).

3. Applied `Licenses` containing the JSON token `"MIT"` and `VersionInfo.IsRelease = true`, deduplicating (both tables contain each row twice), then ranked the surviving projects by parsed fork count.

## Assumptions

- **"project license 'MIT'"** was read as the license recorded on the package version (`packageinfo.Licenses` contains `"MIT"`), not `project_info.Licenses`. Both filters ("license" and "marked as release") live in `packageinfo`. Under the alternative reading (`project_info.Licenses` = `["MIT"]`), the answer would be: mui-org/material-ui (30,522), moment/moment (7,201), semantic-org/semantic-ui (4,955), react-native-elements (4,623), **sveltejs/svelte (4,091)** — i.e. lodash/lodash drops out because its project license is recorded as "non-standard".
- "marked as release" = `VersionInfo.IsRelease` is `true`.
- Join requires exact equality on `System`, `Name`, `Version` (no normalization of version strings).
- Fork counts are taken from the text in `Project_Information`; only the 770 projects present in `project_info` have fork metrics, so projects absent from that table cannot be ranked.

- **Project info coverage**: `project_info` contains 770 distinct projects; projects lacking an entry have no fork count and thus cannot rank.
- **Completeness**: all package names of the top 15 projects by forks (which includes every project above 4,623 forks) were exhaustively checked; the next-highest qualifying project after the top five is sveltejs/svelte at 4,091 forks.

## Method / assumptions

- **Join path:** `packageinfo` (System='NPM') → `project_packageversion` on `System`, `Name`, `Version` → `project_info` by matching the repository path mentioned in the free-text `Project_Information` field (e.g. "The project mui-org/material-ui on GitHub … has 30,522 forks"). `project_info` has no explicit key column, so the `owner/repo` token and the fork count were parsed from that text with regexes (validated: 770/770 rows parsed).
- **"MIT" license** was read from `packageinfo.Licenses` as an exact JSON-array element `"MIT"` (not a substring match), so packages licensed "EPL-2.0 OR MIT" etc. are excluded.

- **Users:** `user.yelping_since` has three mixed date formats (`14 Sep 2016, 00:32`, `September 10, 2016 at 08:02 PM`, `2016-06-23 01:59:28`). All 1,999 parsed successfully with `TRY_STRPTIME`; 168 fall in 2016.
- **Reviews:** `review.date` has the same mixed formats; all parse. Joining reviews to the 2016 cohort and keeping `date >= 2016-01-01` gives 150 reviews over 62 businesses. (Note: those users have **zero** reviews before 2016, so the date filter doesn't change the result.)
- **Categories:** No `categories` field exists. Each `business.description` ends with a prose list of categories (e.g., "…services including Nail Salons, Hair Removal, Beauty & Spas, and Waxing"). I extracted the list for every business and verified all 62 businesses that actually have reviews against the raw description text, character-for-character; a review counts once toward each category its business lists, with duplicates within a description (e.g., "Gas Stations" twice for business 54) counted once.

## Assumptions

1. "Since 2016" means review date ≥ 2016-01-01 (not the user's registration date).
2. "Total reviews from those users" = number of review records written by 2016-registered users, not the business's lifetime `review_count`.
3. Categories are the names listed inside each business's `description`; both broad (e.g., Restaurants, Food, Shopping) and specific categories count, as all are presented as categories in the source text.
4. Lowercase mentions in prose (business 93: "nightlife, bars, restaurants, sports bars") were normalized to the standard category capitalization; this only affects Restaurants/Bars/Nightlife/Sports Bars and does not change the top 5.
5. Reviews with `user_id = 'None'` (null user) are excluded, as they cannot belong to the 2016 cohort.
